arxiv-2001-05011.title: Interval structures in the Bruhat and weak orders Thanks: Research partially supported by Simons Foundation Collaboration Grant for Mathematicians 277603 and by a University Research Council Competitive Research Leave from DePaul University.
arxiv-2001-05011.creator: Bridget Eileen Tenner
arxiv-2001-05011.description: Abstract . We study the appearance of notable interval structures—lattices, modular lattices, distributive lattices, and boolean lattices—in both the Bruhat and weak orders of Coxeter groups. We collect and expand upon known results for principal order ideals, including pattern characterizations and enumerations for the symmetric group.

arxiv-2102-08155.title: Differentiating Surgeon Expertise Solely by Eye Movement Features DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: ETRA ’21: ACM Symposium on Eye Tracking Research Applications ; June 03–05, 2018; Stuttgart, BW Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.
arxiv-2102-08155.creator: Benedikt Hosp, Myat Su Yin, Peter Haddawy, Paphon Sa-Ngasoongsong, Enkelejda Kasneci
arxiv-2102-08155.description: Abstract . Developments in computer science in recent years are moving into hospitals. Surgeons are faced with ever new technical challenges. Visual perception plays a key role in most of these. Diagnostic and training models are needed to optimize the training of young surgeons.

arxiv-2411-01683.title: ROAD-Waymo: Action Awareness at Scale for Autonomous Driving
arxiv-2411-01683.creator: Salman Khan, Izzeddin Teeti, Reza Javanmard Alitappeh, Mihaela C. Stoian, Eleonora Giunchiglia, Gurkirt Singh, Andrew Bradley, Fabio Cuzzolin
arxiv-2411-01683.description: Abstract Autonomous Vehicle (AV) perception systems require more than simply seeing, via e.g., object detection or scene segmentation. They need a holistic understanding of what is happening within the scene for safe interaction with other road users. Few datasets exist for the purpose of developing and training algorithms to comprehend the actions of other road users.

arxiv-2411-03911.title: The crucial discovery of thermonuclear X-ray bursts: never throw away old data! Publication type: Article Type
arxiv-2411-03911.creator: Erik Kuulkers*
arxiv-2411-03911.description: Abstract The detection of Type I X-ray bursts is attributed to those seen by the Astronomical Netherlands Satellite (ANS) in September 1975 from the globular cluster NGC 6624 containing the X-ray source 4U 1820 − - 303. I revisit these X-ray bursts, by re-analysing data from the Soft X-ray Experiment (SXX) onboard ANS, which were stored on microfiche.

arxiv-2412-19920.title: Not all Views are Created Equal: Analyzing Viewpoint Instabilities in Vision Foundation Models
arxiv-2412-19920.creator: Mateusz Michalkiewicz, Sheena Bai, Mahsa Baktashmotlagh, Varun Jampani, Guha Balakrishnan
arxiv-2412-19920.description: Abstract In this paper, we analyze the viewpoint stability of foundational models - specifically, their sensitivity to changes in viewpoint- and define instability as significant feature variations resulting from minor changes in viewing angle, leading to generalization gaps in 3D reasoning tasks.

arxiv-2503-09966.title: More about quark Yukawa textures from selection rules without group actions
arxiv-2503-09966.creator: Tatsuo Kobayashi 1, Yume Nishioka 1, Hajime Otsuka 2 , and, Morimitsu Tanimoto 3
arxiv-2503-09966.description: Abstract We study the coupling selection rules associated with non-group symmetries, i.e., ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2} gauging of ℤ M \mathbb{Z}_{M} symmetries. We clarify which Yukawa textures can be derived by our selection rules for M = 3 , 4 M=3,4 , and 5, and obtain various textures including the nearest neighbor interaction type and its extension.

arxiv-2507-15242.creator: Guo-Yu Li, Da-Bin Lin, Zhi-Lin Chen, En-Wei Liang
arxiv-2507-15242.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guo-Yu Li, Da-Bin Lin, Zhi-Lin Chen, En-Wei Liang. The prompt γ \gamma -rays of gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) may originate from the photosphere of a relativistic jet. However, only a few GRBs have been observed with evident blackbody-like emission, for example, GRB 090902B. It has been demonstrated that internal dissipation processes, such as magnetic reconnection, can occur within the relativistic jet and thereby drive violent turbulence in the dissipation region.

arxiv-2507-19718.title: GSCache: Real-Time Radiance Caching for Volume Path Tracing using 3D Gaussian Splatting
arxiv-2507-19718.creator: \authororcid David Bauer0000-0002-1327-3054, \authororcid Qi Wu0000-0003-0342-9366, \authororcid Hamid Gadirov0000-0001-6578-4342, and \authororcid Kwan-Liu Ma0000-0001-8086-0366
arxiv-2507-19718.description: Abstract Real-time path tracing is rapidly becoming the standard for rendering in entertainment and professional applications. In scientific visualization, volume rendering plays a crucial role in helping researchers analyze and interpret complex 3D data. Recently, photorealistic rendering techniques have gained popularity in scientific visualization, yet they face significant challenges.

arxiv-2512-18412.title: Few-Shot Learning of a Graph-Based Neural Network Model Without Backpropagation
arxiv-2512-18412.creator: Mykyta Lapin, Kostiantyn Bokhan, Yurii Parzhyn
arxiv-2512-18412.description: Abstract Subject. We propose a structural-graph approach to classifying contour images in a few-shot regime without using backpropagation. The core idea is to make structure the carrier of explanations: an image is encoded as an attributed graph (critical points and lines represented as nodes with geometric attributes), and generalization is achieved via the formation of concept attractors (class-level concept graphs).

arxiv-2602-15961.description: Abstract . The rapid expansion of renewable energy, particularly wind and solar power, has made reliable forecasting critical for power system operations. While recent deep learning models have achieved strong average accuracy, the increasing frequency and intensity of climate-driven extreme weather events pose severe threats to grid stability and operational security.

pmc-10572994.title: Endoscopic Ultrasound in Pancreatic Duct Anomalies
pmc-10572994.creator: Abhirup Chatterjee, Surinder Singh Rana, Hajime Isomoto, Fabiano Bini
pmc-10572994.description: Embryological development of the pancreas is a complex phenomenon and, therefore, it can have multiple developmental aberrations. Fortunately, the majority of these pancreatic ductal anomalies are asymptomatic with no clinical relevance and are incidentally detected during diagnostic cross-sectional imaging or endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) or autopsy. Occasionally, pancreatic duct anomalies can result in symptoms like abdominal pain or recurrent pancreatitis.

pmc-10622543.title: Patient-derived organoids identify tailored therapeutic options and determinants of plasticity in sarcomatoid urothelial bladder cancer
pmc-10622543.creator: Michele Garioni, Viviane J. Tschan, Lauriane Blukacz, Sandro Nuciforo, Romuald Parmentier, Luca Roma, Mairene Coto-Llerena, Heike Pueschel, Salvatore Piscuoglio, Tatjana Vlajnic, Frank Stenner, Hans-Helge Seifert, Cyrill A. Rentsch, Lukas Bubendorf, Clémentine Le Magnen
pmc-10622543.description: Sarcomatoid Urothelial Bladder Cancer (SARC) is a rare and aggressive histological subtype of bladder cancer for which therapeutic options are limited and experimental models are lacking. Here, we report the establishment of a long-term 3D organoid-like model derived from a SARC patient (SarBC-01).

pmc-10671118.title: IbINV Positively Regulates Resistance to Black Rot Disease Caused by Ceratocystis fimbriata in Sweet Potato
pmc-10671118.creator: Dongjing Yang, Xiaofeng Bian, Ho Soo Kim, Rong Jin, Fangyuan Gao, Jingwei Chen, Jukui Ma, Wei Tang, Chengling Zhang, Houjun Sun, Yiping Xie, Zongyun Li, Sang-Soo Kwak, Daifu Ma
pmc-10671118.description: Black rot disease, caused by Ceratocystis fimbriata Ellis & Halsted, severely affects both plant growth and post-harvest storage of sweet potatoes. Invertase (INV) enzymes play essential roles in hydrolyzing sucrose into glucose and fructose and participate in the regulation of plant defense responses.

pmc-11510740.title: The Effect of Larval Exposure to Heavy Metals on the Gut Microbiota Composition of Adult Anopheles arabiensis (Diptera: Culicidae)
pmc-11510740.creator: Ashmika Singh, Shristi Misser, Mushal Allam, Wai-Yin Chan, Arshad Ismail, Givemore Munhenga, Shüné V Oliver, Eliningaya J Kweka
pmc-11510740.description: Anopheles arabiensis is a highly adaptable member of the An. gambiae complex. Its flexible resting behaviour and diverse feeding habits make conventional vector control methods less effective in controlling this species. Another emerging challenge is its adaptation to breeding in polluted water, which impacts various life history traits relevant to epidemiology.

pmc-12534921.title: Implementation Strategies Applied in Communities Matching Process (ISAC Match): Expanded Guidance and Case Study
pmc-12534921.creator: Laura E Balis, Taren Massey-Swindle, Shelly Palmer, Emily Shaw, Shelby Jones-Dozier, Michelle Grocke-Dewey
pmc-12534921.description: BackgroundImplementation strategies are methods or techniques to improve the adoption, implementation, sustainment, and scale-up of evidence-based interventions. Limited guidance exists on feasible processes for selecting and tailoring implementation strategies in community (non-clinical) settings. The Implementation Strategies Applied in Communities (ISAC) compilation includes a pragmatic matching process to accompany the compilation (ISAC Match).

pmc-12623313.title: Rejected by an AI? Comparing job applicants’ fairness perceptions of artificial intelligence and humans in personnel selection
pmc-12623313.creator: Christine Malin, Jürgen Fleiß, Renate Ortlieb, Stefan Thalmann
pmc-12623313.description: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) transforms personnel selection, but the application of AI raises fairness concerns and aversion towards AI. Although job applicants may perceive the selection process as fairer when they receive an explanation for the decision, scientific knowledge about AI-related fairness perceptions in this setting is limited.

pmc-13122875.title: Coupled mesoporous silica nanoparticles and limonene–chitosan Pickering emulsions: enhanced insecticidal delivery and selectivity
pmc-13122875.creator: Nannan Lv, Zhixuan Xu, Qingyang Zhang, Xinyu Wang, Yunxuan Wu, Ren Li, Jianting Fan
pmc-13122875.description: BackgroundNanodelivery represents a promising strategy to enhance pesticide efficacy while reducing associated environmental risks. Mesoporous silica nanospheres (MSNs) can serve as effective nanocarriers but improvements are essential in terms of targeting and efficiency. A promising approach involves combining nanocarriers-mediated pesticide delivery system with bioactive compounds, in which the compounds act as synergist that can disrupt insect defence mechanisms.

pmc-13679153.title: A risk management intervention in Australian hospital food service departments: an evaluation using the RE-AIM framework
pmc-13679153.creator: Jodi Oakman, Jasmine Love, Joanne Marcucci
pmc-13679153.description: BackgroundThe RE-AIM (reach, effectiveness, adoption, implementation, maintenance) framework was used to undertake a process evaluation of a workplace intervention using the A Participative Hazard Identification and Risk Management (APHIRM) Toolkit. The aim of the intervention was to reduce work-related physical and psychosocial hazards associated with musculoskeletal disorders and stress related mental health in hospital food services employees.
